extracted.intended_audience: Researchers considering or preparing ERC grant applications (EU and non-EU)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the main ERC funding opportunities, their target applicants and key eligibility/selection characteristics, plus pointers to resources (work programme, national contact points, FAQs, explanatory videos).

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Starting Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 2-7 years of experience since the completion of their PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target group: early-career researchers 2–7 years post-PhD; selection emphasises both an already promising track record and the quality/excellence of the research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Consolidator Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 7-12 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target group: mid-career researchers 7–12 years post-PhD; applicants should demonstrate promise in their scientific track record and submit an excellent research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Advanced Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for active researchers with a track-record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target group: senior/established researchers; evaluation focuses on significant recent research achievements over the past decade and continued active research leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Proof of Concept
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers who have already received an ERC grant for their frontier research project and now want to explore the commercial or societal potential of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires prior ERC funding; purpose is to support exploration of commercialisation or societal impact of already-funded ERC research.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Synergy Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for two to maximum four researchers working together and bringing different skills and resources to tackle ambitious research problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team-based funding: 2–4 PIs combining complementary skills and resources; emphasis on collaborative approaches to ambitious problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional opportunities linked to ERC funding
rubrics_metrics.description: There are other initiatives linked to ERC funding. If you are not planning to apply for a grant, or it’s too early to, you may still be interested in these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants or interested researchers should consider supplementary ERC-linked initiatives as alternative engagement routes even if not ready to apply for a main grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: National contact points
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one based in every EU and Associated Country, as well as in some countries outside Europe. They are designated to help applicants out in their own countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to contact their national contact point as an early step for country-specific help and guidance on ERC applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents and publications to consult (Work Programme and Information for Applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are considering applying, you'll have several key documents to refer to, like the Work Programme and the Information for Applicants. These highlight the specifics of the calls every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult the Work Programme and Information for Applicants for call-specific rules, eligibility, application details and useful preparatory information before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a question about your ERC application? Throughout the years, we have collected some of the most frequently asked questions to guide you through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the FAQs to find answers to common application questions and clarifications on procedures and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance videos (Step-by-step and ERC Classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a short introduction to ERC grants, watch our step-by-step video. ERC Classes: a series of 5 explanatory videos giving concrete information about the ERC application process, including frequently made mistakes, tips and rumours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these videos for an accessible introduction to the application process; ERC Classes specifically address common mistakes and practical tips for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for non-EU researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a researcher from outside the EU and you wish to apply check out some of the things you should consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-EU applicants should review specific considerations affecting eligibility, institutional arrangements or administrative steps relevant to applicants based outside the EU/Associated Countries.
